notes: 32,200,000. A label rather than a person, which `creator` already covers — `creator:yg` was refused as a two-character *tag*, not because a label is not a creator.
7,060,000. A news organisation. Kept because a subscription to it is a real act; note it says nothing about politics, and no `refusedTopics` entry is bypassed by minting the channel itself.
4,380,000. Was aliased to `subject:science` and should not have been — the name is the term.
1,680,000. Was aliased to `subject:statistics`, and the tokens `Josh` and `Starmer` were the ones that nearly landed this channel on a musician.
1,460,000. Taiwanese comedy. The channel this whole rule was argued from: it was called an ambiguous string and it is a professional entity with a million and a half subscribers.
1,210,000. Taiwanese science media. Was aliased to `subject:science`.
718,000. Taiwanese comedy troupe. Key romanised because concept keys are ASCII; the exact title is the alias, as `creator:one_ok_rock` does for ワンオク.
713,000. Keyed on the channel rather than on the person, because this ontology has no separate concept for her and minting one from a channel title would assert an identity the data does not state.
